title: introduce-tenant-consent-ledger-and-tiered-audit-sampling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds tenant consent ledger for operator actions, configurable tiered audit sampling, and lightweight KMS consent tagging. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Customers running in regulated environments have asked for stronger evidence that operator/automation actions performed on tenant resources are both consented to and auditable without exploding storage/ingest costs. This PR introduces a lightweight Tenant Consent Ledger plus a tiered audit sampling mechanism that attaches consent proof to KMS-wrapped operation metadata when available and selects full-audit vs sampled records based on policy.

Summary of changes: implemented a new ledger service (consent-ledger) that records concise consent assertions (tenant_id, actor, scope, consent_nonce, timestamp, consent_ttl, decision_hash) and exposes a read API for compliance tooling. Added policy-controlled tiered sampling to audit forwarder: critical operations (key unwrap, operator impersonation, credential-issuance) are fully recorded; medium-risk ops get deterministic sampled attachments (1/10 by default) with opt-in for broader capture; low-risk ops stay aggregated. Consent assertions are cryptographically referenced in audit events via a consent_token (HMAC over ledger id + timestamp) and optionally anchored to KMS envelopes when a CMK is used.

Design notes: ledger entries are compact and immutable. Ledger storage is sharded by tenant geozone to respect residency constraints and routed by existing residency-decider. Consent TTL allows automatic expiry; expired ledger entries return a 410-like response from read API but remain in append-only store for retention/audit. Tiered sampling rules are policy-driven, configurable per tenant namespace with defaults in defaults/compliance.yaml. The change is behind feature flags: feature.consensus.ledger.enabled and feature.audit.tiered_sampling.enabled for safe rollout.

Commit summary: - Add consent-ledger service and migrations (db schema + golang service glue) - Implement consent token HMAC helper and KMS-envelope attach routine - Extend audit-forwarder to include consent_token field and tiered-sampling policy evaluation - Add residency-aware sharding logic and integration tests - Add e2e compliance test harness and docs + console feature flag UI wiring

Files touched (high level): - services/consent-ledger/* (new) - internal/audit/forwarder.go (sampling logic, consent_token attach) - internal/kms/attach.go (optional consent envelope attach) - migrations/20251103_create_consent_ledger.sql - docs/compliance/consent-ledger.md - console/src/features/featureFlags/ConsentLedgerToggle.tsx - tests/integration/consent-ledger-e2e.test.go

Small illustrative snippet (audit event): "{"op":"operator_rotate_key","tenant_id":"t-123","consent_token":"ct_2b9f...","audit_level":"full"}"

Review conversation (high level, chronological): 
- Miguel Santos: "Can we avoid a second DB connection for the ledger in short-lived processes (workers)? Consider using the existing shard pool; also validate retention config per-tenant."
- Aisha Patel (author): "Updated to reuse shard pool and added tenant_retention_days config with guardrails. See migration and shard pool wiring in commit 3/6."
- Claire Wong: "Tests look good, but we need to ensure consent_token doesn't leak sensitive info to downstream analytics. Please add sanitization in audit-forwarder and document expected safe fields."
- Aisha Patel: "Sanitization added, forwarder now strips consent_token in analytics path while keeping it in compliance logs. Note documented in docs/compliance/consent-ledger.md."
- Ethan Berger: "Behavior under KMS unavailability? Should fallback to recording ledger-only and mark event as 'consent_unanchored' so downstream processes treat it differently."
- Aisha Patel: "Added consent_unanchored flag and updated fallback path with retries (3x) and a fast-path ledger-only store. Tests added for KMS failures."
- Miguel Santos: "Approved after addressing DB pooling and the analytics sanitization notes."

CI and checks: "CI initially failed on a flaky integration test (TestConsentLedger_EvictExpired) caused by time-sensitive assertion. I pinned the test to use mock clock and re-ran. All checks: unit (pass), integration (pass after fix), lint (pass), e2e (pass), security-scan (pass)."

Rollout plan and migration: "The migration is additive. DB migration adds a new consent_ledger table with tenant_id index and geozone shard key. Rollout plan: 1) deploy service + migrations in read-only mode, 2) enable feature flag for a small % of tenants, 3) monitor audit volume and consent-mismatch alerts, 4) increase tenant coverage, 5) flip default on. Console toggle added for enterprise operators. Backfill utility included to import consent assertions from legacy traces when available."

Backward compatibility: "Audit schema gains an optional consent_token string and consent_unanchored boolean; consumers must tolerate absence of consent fields. Default sampling policy preserves previous behavior for tenants without the feature flag."

Security considerations: "Consent tokens are HMACed with a service-side secret stored in Vault and rotated via standard key rotation. Consent ledger access is RBAC-protected (new role: roles/compliance.reader and roles/compliance.writer) and enforced in policy compiler mapping. KMS anchoring uses existing CMK policies; if KMS anchoring fails, ledger-only entries are recorded and marked. Sensitive fields are redacted before analytics export. Added audit policy test vectors to the compliance test harness."

Merge outcome: "Merged to main via squash merge after approvals. Feature flags default to off. Follow-up work includes a small operator UX polish (console notices) and a metrics dashboard to show sampled vs full audit ratios (ENG-2403)."
commit_summaries: feat(consent-ledger): add ledger service and db migration
feat(audit): tiered sampling evaluation and consent_token attach
fix(tests): use mock clock for eviction test
chore(console): add feature flag toggle UI
docs(compliance): document ledger semantics and rollout
notes_for_ops: Ensure vault/consent_hmac_secret is available in the deployment environment
Migration should be run during low-traffic window; table is append-only and indexed by tenant_id+geozone
If KMS anchor latency spikes, audit-forwarder will mark consent_unanchored; SLOs unaffected but compliance workflow should be alerted
